subject: Request: headroom credits + failover 'ride-along' for reserved GPUs
messages:
From: Sofia Alvarez <s.alvarez@chroniclecap.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@chroniclecap.com>
Date: 2026-08-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Headroom credits and failover behavior for reserved GPUs

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the call last week — Chronicle Capital is close to finalizing committed reserved nodes with Redwood. Before procurement signs the order, our infra and platform teams have one last ask around capacity guarantees and operational behavior during transient congestion. Two items in particular:

1) Headroom credit accumulation: we run erratic bursty inference patterns tied to end-of-day batch scoring. We need a clear mechanism by which small, unused capacity during quiet hours accrues as credits that can be spent during spikes without penalty. Can Redwood define how headroom credits would be tracked and consumed, and whether credits carry across billing cycles?

2) Failover 'ride-along' policy: if reserved GPUs are temporarily preempted for maintenance or reclaimed for autoscaling, Chronicle needs the option for a subset of live requests to be routed to compatible best-effort nodes without triggering throttles or billing surprises. Essentially a short-duration ride-along to preserve latency for high-priority routes.

We'd like these behaviors codified as an addendum to the reserved capacity agreement (preferably with sample SLIs and a short runbook for incident handoff). I've attached a CSV showing typical hourly demand (chronicle_demand_graphs.csv) to help illustrate our pattern.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide an addendum draft and a short observability runbook that details queueing visibility and metrics we should monitor?

Thanks,
Sofia Alvarez
Head of Platform Engineering
Chronicle Capital

--
Attachment: chronicle_demand_graphs.csv (CSV, 48KB)

Hi Sofia — thanks for the detailed notes and the attachment. Great to see the demand profile; it helps a lot.

Short answers up front: yes, we can propose a formal addendum with both a headroom-credit mechanism and a controlled failover ride-along. We'd like to propose a short working session with Ben (serving/runtime) and Irene (account lead) to align on the exact SLI thresholds and the operational cadence for credits.

Proposed next steps:
- Ben and I will draft a 1-page technical annex that defines: credit accrual calculation, max credit bank per reserved pool, expiration policy, and billing treatment during consumption.
- Ben will also propose an implementation approach for the ride-along: policy controls, tagging of high-priority routes, and preemption grace windows.
- We will share a first-pass addendum (PDF) and an observability runbook (MD) by EOD Friday.

Can you do a 30-minute sync on Thursday 8/19 at 11:00 AM PT? If not, propose another slot.

Thanks — Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Success, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Alvarez <s.alvarez@chroniclecap.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-18T13:34:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Headroom credits and failover behavior for reserved GPUs (technical details and draft addendum)

Hi Sofia, Kim — following our internal scoping, attaching a first-pass addendum and a short runbook to illustrate behavior. See proposed highlights below; the attachments include the exact legal-friendly language and sample observability queries.

Summary (technical):
- Credit accrual: We propose measuring headroom on a per-reservation pool basis at 5-minute intervals. For each interval, any unused reserved concurrency (measured as reserved tokens/sec minus consumed tokens/sec) contributes to the customer's credit bank. Credits are denominated in 'token-minutes' and accumulate up to a cap equal to 48 hours worth of average reserved throughput. Credits expire after 90 days.

- Consumption & billing: When credits are spent during a spike, those tokens are consumed from the credit bank first; consumption uses the customer's normal reserved pricing (no surprise overage rate). If credits are exhausted, standard burst pricing applies. We will surface credit balance as a metric in the Console (credit_balance_token_minutes).

- Ride-along failover: For a configurable subset of routes (tagged as high-priority), requests may be temporarily routed to compatible best-effort backends for up to a 10-minute window per preemption event. During ride-along windows: latency SLAs are suspended and we commit to preserving request ordering and KV-cache warm-start hints where available. Billing for ride-along traffic will be drawn from the headroom credit pool first; if no credits remain, we default to reserved pricing for the first 2 minutes and then to burst pricing thereafter.

- Observability: The runbook contains sample PromQL and Console queries for: queue depth per pool, wait-time percentiles (p50/p95/p99), preemption event count, and credit_balance_token_minutes. We recommend instrumenting two alert rules: (a) credit_balance <= 20% of cap and (b) ride-along events > 3 in a 24h window.

- Edge cases: We document behavior during multi-pool failovers and for pinned-node reservations (we avoid cross-pool credit consumption unless explicitly enabled in the addendum).

Attachments: proposed_addendum_draft.pdf (language + SLI table), observability_runbook_v1.md (queries + runbook).

If these terms look acceptable, we can 1) update the legal wording based on your feedback, and 2) lock in a pilot for 30 days to validate credit accounting and ride-along routing on a single reserved pool. For the pilot we'd need a short run of traffic instrumentation and one production maintenance window to exercise failover behavior.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

--

Kim, Ben — thanks for the thorough response and the draft materials. The credit model and the ride-along proposal look reasonable to Chronicle. A few quick clarifications before legal signs:

- Can you confirm the exact Prometheus label names for credit_balance_token_minutes and ride_along_event_count so our monitoring team can wire alerts now?
- For the pilot, can Redwood schedule the maintenance window during our low-traffic weekday window (Mon–Thu 02:00–05:00 PT)? We prefer not to run the pilot during our heavy batch windows.

Assuming those clarifications are fine, procurement is prepared to execute the addendum and run the 30-day pilot. Please send a DocuSign link for CHC-4821 and we'll route to legal.

Best,
Sofia Alvarez
Head of Platform Engineering
Chronicle Capital
